blockers.quote: Row three. The night batch. You, copying the topper's notes. Like every night.
blockers.why: story #2: at 115 words a minute this line runs almost the whole first 7 seconds, so I am still watching you copy notes. The thumbnail I clicked is the shocked face beside the crimson 0.04% chip, and that picture (line 20) starts only after this line plus line 19, near 12 seconds.
blockers.fix: Row three. Copying. Like every night. Replace line 19 with: Over every head.

blockers.quote: A year of fees. A year of your life. On one chair. So... keep going?
blockers.why: story #3: this line starts at about 0:31 and 'a year of your life' lands nearer 0:36, after 56 earlier words, the 0.2s opening hold and the 2s hold on line 29. By 0:30 I can say the title question and 'one chair out of two thousand five hundred.' The year I can lose is still ahead.
blockers.fix: Keep this line after the chair. Replace line 29 with: > HOLD: 0.5 s. The one crimson chair pulses once. Use the shorter opening in the story #2 fix so this line starts near 0:23.

blockers.quote: > HOLD: 2.5 s. The bus rolls through streets of chips, no numerals: a woman jogging, her chip brightening with each stride; a boy asleep on a shop counter, his dimming.
blockers.why: The viewer's week: this is the line where I stop. The jogger and the boy on the counter are outside my week (chai, the bus, exams, the office, family). The bus rolls and nothing happens to me.
blockers.fix: > HOLD: 2.5 s. The bus rolls past the coaching centre, the chai stall and your lane: chips only over the teacher, the topper, the chaiwala and Aarav.

suggestions.quote: Here's how it works. Each chip is one person's chance at the one thing they'd choose... with nobody watching. It never tells you what that thing is.
suggestions.fix: Each chip is the thing they'd choose with nobody watching, and it moves when they do.

suggestions.quote: You've been wearing the crowd's number. Like a verdict.
suggestions.fix: Replace lines 89 to 91 with one line: Copying their notes never copied their number. Yours moved down.

suggestions.quote: Your own number moves. You've seen it. His... you just read.
suggestions.fix: Yours changes when you work. His, you only read.

keep.quote: One chair. Out of two thousand five hundred.
You can't borrow someone's odds. Only their apron.
The biggest number? It tells you what's likely. It can't tell you what's worth choosing.
